q: None of the above-auction happens when Railway sells scrap; Reverse Auction happens

options.B: When Suppliers bid to become L1

e: Option C (When Railway counters suppliers bids) is the correct choice. Option (C) is correct: in a reverse auction, suppliers progressively bid prices down to become L1, and the Railway counters the suppliers' bids to drive the price lower. This is the mirror image of a forward auction, where the Railway sells scrap and buyers bid the price up. Related exam fact: reverse auction is a procurement tool used to obtain the lowest competitive price from willing suppliers.

q: Stores budget is a ‘derived’ budget because

options.A: Stores department does not have its own budget
options.B: Stores department budgets for all other departments
options.C: All revenue and workshop stock items requirements are compiled in Stores budget

e: The Stores budget is called a 'derived' budget because the Stores department does not have a budget of its own; it budgets for all other departments, compiling all revenue and workshop stock item requirements in the Stores budget. Hence, all of the above.

q: Make in India Policy stipulates that complete purchase shall be made only fromlocal firms

options.A: If tender value is less than 50 lakhs
options.B: If tender value is more than 50 lakhs
options.C: If tender value is less than 25 lakhs
options.D: If tender value is more than 25 lakhs

e: If tender value is more than 25 lakhs — that is the right answer. Option (D) is correct: under the Make in India public-procurement preference policy, complete purchase is to be made only from local firms when the tender value is more than Rs. 25 lakh. Higher-value tenders are thus reserved for domestic suppliers to promote indigenous manufacturing. Related exam fact: the policy classifies local suppliers (Class-I, Class-II) based on the percentage of local content in the item.

q: Security Deposit is to be deposited in which of the following forms?
e: Option (D) is correct: security deposit is deposited in the form of a cheque or a demand draft — hence 'a and b'. It is the contractor's guarantee for due performance of the contract and is distinct from the earnest money deposited with the tender. Earnest money (with the tender) shows the bidder's seriousness; the security deposit (from the contractor) guards against default. Remember: Watch the timeline or sequence in such questions; many errors come from mixing up the order.

q: Option Clause in Stores contracts enables Railway to place an order of 30%above or below the PO quantity

options.B: Supplier can request this additional quantity
options.C: Railway has to take supplier’s consent
options.D: A separate negotiation has to be done for this quantity

e: Option (B) is correct: under the option clause, which lets the Railway vary the order by 30% above or below the PO quantity, it is the supplier who can request this additional quantity — the Railway does not enforce it unilaterally or negotiate it separately. An audit para is a formal audit observation; paras are settled through compliance, recovery or regularisation. Remember: Note the exact terminology used — the exam rewards precise vocabulary.

q: The difference between time/tally sheet and labour Pay 13 sheet on average rate is allocated to
e: Option (B) is correct: the difference between the time/tally sheet and the labour (Pay 13) sheet on average rate is allocated to Shop on cost. Such differences arise from idle time and average-rate adjustments and are treated as workshop overhead. Oncost (overhead) collects indirect expenses — supervision, power, consumables — and allocates them to jobs on a suitable base like direct labour hours.

q: Work orders which conform to Revenue Accounting Classification and remainunchanged from year to year are called
e: Option (C) is correct: work orders which conform to the Revenue Accounting Classification and remain unchanged from year to year are called Revenue Standing work orders. A work order is the written authority for a workshop job; all labour, material and oncost for that job are booked against its number for costing. Remember: Watch the timeline or sequence in such questions; many errors come from mixing up the order.

q: The proposal sent by Zonal Railway to Railway Board for specific need of Rolling Stock is called:-
e: Option (B) is correct: the proposal sent by a Zonal Railway to the Railway Board for its specific requirement of rolling stock is called the Itemized Rolling Stock programme. It details the numbers and types of locos, coaches and wagons the zone needs. The Railway Board is the apex body of Indian Railways, exercising powers over policy, finance and administration for the whole system. Remember: Watch the timeline or sequence in such questions; many errors come from mixing up the order.

q: When PSC sleepers is supplied by authorised firm to private party they pay
e: Inspection Charges to Railways. — that is the right answer. Option (A) is correct: when PSC sleepers are supplied by an authorised firm to a private party, the party pays Inspection Charges to the Railways. Railway inspection certifies that the sleepers meet specifications, and the cost of that inspection is recovered as charges. Related exam fact: inspection by the Railway's inspecting agency is the quality assurance mechanism for materials manufactured to railway-approved designs for outside parties.

q: Which of the following statements are correct? The stock adjustment account is operated to for recording differences arising out of :- a. Variation in stock noticed on account of Stock Verification or DepartmentalStock Verification. b. Changes in Price of stock purchased from market or manufactured at workshop. c. Difference in book value and actual value realised on Scrap sale d. Rounding off

options.A: only I and ii are correct
options.B: only I, ii and iii are correct
options.D: only I and iii are correct

e: Option C (all are correct) is the correct choice. Option (C) is correct: the stock adjustment account is operated to record differences arising from all four causes — variations found on stock verification, changes in the price of stock purchased or manufactured, the difference between book value and actual value realised on scrap sale, and rounding off. Hence 'all are correct'. Related exam fact: the account bridges the gap between book balances and the physical and financial realities of stores holdings.
